\[
\hat{R} = m + W\,(z - m),
\qquad
W = \max\Bigl(0,\; \frac{1 - C_u^2 / C_I^2}{1 + C_u^2}\Bigr)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m\): The window mean
- \(C_I\): The coefficient of variation of the window
- \(C_u\): The coefficient of variation of the speckle
- \(W\): The weight of the pixel

m is the window mean and C_I its coefficient of variation. Kuan, Sawchuk, Strand and Chavel turn the multiplicative noise into a signal-dependent additive noise and derive the linear minimum mean-square error weight without the linear approximation of Lee. The result is the Lee weight divided by 1 + C_u squared, as Lopes, Touzi and Nezry write it.
